findings: Eliminating local oscillator displacement gives the exact frequency-dependent inertial response for the host scattering problem. It does not replace the separate host kinetic, host strain, attached-mass kinetic and spring energy terms of the microscopic Hamiltonian.

The complete shortcut retains exact reflection, transmission, standing-wave interference and field integrals. Its positive nondispersive energy closure omits internal stored energy while preserving the calibrated resonator-free limit.

The fixed below-resonance range keeps the effective inertia positive and the scattering problem regular. Lead continuity and radiation boundaries match the independent coupled finite-element equations.
A traveling-wave scattering derivation and direct quadrature of all four mechanical energy terms agree with the oracle; coupled finite elements converge independently.

The public model and total mechanical energy of the specified slab region determine the observable without supplying the dispersive energy correction or mandating elimination, quadrature or finite elements.
